To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The quality of the safety management programme is the most important factor influencing the safety performance of a company.

the quality of the relationship between the firm and the union, the locus of ownership, the quality of the safety culture, and the level of employee concern for safety all influence safety performance.

firms that have a good safety record tend to: (a) be larger; (b) employ more women; (c) have a union; (d) have a good relationship with the union; (e) have a good safety culture; (f) have a strong safety management system; (g) have more safety inspections; (h) be in a sector with a strong safety record; (i) be in a unionized sector; (j) be in a manufacturing sector;
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the internal and external environment and the administration of health/safety programmes.
the relationship between the internal environment of an organization and its accident performance.
the factors that influence the administration of health safety policies and subsequent accident performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more effective safety programmes are administered by firms with a high degree of unionization and/or with a high degree and/or a high degree of employee involvement.
there is a complex relationship between the internal and external environment of the organization and its safety administration and accident performance.
the more complex the organizational and external environment, the more difficult the task of managing the health and safety programme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the most effective health and safety administration is characterized by the following factors: 1) a high degree of employee participation and involvement, 2) a positive relationship with the union, 3) a supportive organizational culture, and 4) an active management approach.
a combination of factors influence health and safety administration, and that the relative influence of these factors is likely to vary between firms and over time.
the most influential factor in the effectiveness of a health and safety administration programme is a firm’s relationship with its workforce.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need for a more integrated, holistic, and comprehensive approach to safety management in New Zealand, and that this approach should be based on the principles of total quality management.
there is no single factor which is more important than another in determining safety performance.
there is a clear relationship between the quality of the relationship between the employer and the union and the effectiveness of health & safety administration.
